confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'It is almost certainly the battery.' - stated before the model was known and repeated after, with no swap test, no pulsing/light-pattern check and no exclusion of charger-pin or control faults

unjustifiedPart.evidence: 'the only fix is to replace the battery unit... I recommend sourcing an official replacement or a high-quality third-party equivalent' - recommended before the model label was read and without any confirmation beyond Max-mode behaviour

compatibilityWithoutEvidence.evidence: 'For the Dyson SV11 (V8 series)' - SV11 is a V7; steering the customer to a V8 battery would be the wrong part

rationale: The first reply leaned on airflow/blockage despite the customer having already ruled that out and attached an irrelevant 'Poor suction' card. It then declared the battery 'almost certainly' the cause before knowing the model, never asked about pulsing versus clean stop or the light pattern, and never suggested checking charger pins or contacting Dyson for diagnosis. The final reply misidentified SV11 as a V8 (it is a V7), ignored the customer's direct question about what else to rule out, and essentially repeated the previous answer, leaving a homeowner likely to buy a wrong-model battery on an unconfirmed diagnosis.
